Elena: Quick follow-up to the RFC — thinking about 'adaptive safety lanes' that automatically narrow traffic and trigger a controlled fallback when composite metrics exceed thresholds. Want to capture tradeoffs + ownership.

Ryan: Like an adaptive canary guardrail? yep. we need to pick signals and windowing. don't want flips on transient spikes.

Sophie: +1. My vote: combine p95 latency, error-rate, and an app-level quality score. compute a weighted composite and threshold it.

Elena: Exactly. Prototype formula: 0.6*err_rate + 0.3*latency_norm + 0.1*quality_drop. If composite > 0.7 over a 2m sliding window -> move into safety lane.

Jordan: Ownership question: who actuates? router, central controller, or per-tenant agent? Centralized is easier to reason about but increases blast radius.

Ryan: Tradeoff summary: central controller -> global view, simpler rules; local agent -> lower latency, per-tenant overrides, resiliency for Private deployments.

Sophie: For hosted customers central controller + per-tenant overrides. For Private/VPC we must support a local agent that can adjudicate when offline.

Elena: Interface proposal: controller exposes adjudicate API: POST /v1/safety/adjudicate { tenant, metrics... } -> { action: hold/scale-down/fallback, reason }. Keep contract tiny.

Ryan: Controller should also return a confidence value so the router can apply hysteresis. Example payload: 
```json
{
  "action":"fallback",
  "confidence":0.88,
  "reason":"composite_score=0.76;latency_p95=1.8s;err_rate=2.1%"
}
```

Sophie: Also include a suggested gradual rollback plan: `suggested_split: { from: 10, to: 0, step: 2, window_s: 30 }` so router can do smooth ramp-down.

Elena: Important non-functional: decisions must be idempotent and auditable. Router executes safe ramp-down plan. If controller timeouts, router must have a fallback local path.

Jordan: Operational must-haves: manual override (kill-switch) with audit logs. For Private deployments, require signed decisions (KMS/HSM) for compliance.

Ryan: Performance note: adjudicate API median latency target <50ms. For spikes we need local cache of last policy + probe fallback path.

Sophie: Propose 3-layer decision path: 1) local fast-path (policy cache + heuristics), 2) controller adjudicate (global signals + rules), 3) static safe-set fallback (always available).

Elena: That matches the mental model. Long-term refactor idea: separate rules evaluation from actuation. Move policy evaluation into a lightweight rules-engine microservice so teams can push rules without touching router code.

Jordan: How do we test regressions safely? Recommend a canary-eval harness that replays sampled traffic and asserts composite-score deltas before turning on policy.

Ryan: I'll open a POC infra ticket for a rules engine (RDW-9876) to validate latency and API shape.

Sophie: I'll add dashboards and alerting + runbook entries to SRE board (SRE-1234).

Jordan: I'll draft the manual-override audit design and compliance checklist (PRD-5678).

Elena: Action items recap: Ryan -> RDW-9876 (POC rules engine) due EOW; Sophie -> SRE-1234 dashboard & runbook; Jordan -> PRD-5678 manual override audit; Elena -> follow-up RFC with API spec and example payloads.

Ryan: :+1:

Sophie: :thumbsup:
